correctness.rationale: For target-rooted finite tree, a non-backtracking oriented arrival p(v)→v has expected first parent-return time F_v=2b_v−1 by induction: child excursions cost 2b_w and the linear child-arrival equations give U_w=1+2(k S_v−b_w)/(k+1), S_v=b_v−1, k=d_v−1. Fresh-start parent passage B_v=1+2kS_v/(k+1) handles the first step. Strong Markov decomposition along source-target path and SRW parent passage A_v=2b_v−1 give the exact difference 2[(b_s−1)/d_s+Σ_{i=1}^{ℓ−1}(b_{v_i}−1+b_{v_{i−1}})/d_{v_i}]. Every summand nonnegative and each intermediate strictly positive, so equality iff s leaf directly adjacent target. Independently rebuilt lifted directed-edge linear systems on 96 ordered-pair checks of finite trees, agreeing with formula. Uniform first neighbor, deterministic leaf reflection, and no-cycle hypotheses are essential.
